specification.objective: Replace the accumulated Kanban frontend experiments with one clean, SDK-only architecture. Remove the previous Kanban UI/rendering/diagnostic work, retain only objectively validated backend/domain contracts, separate Kanban state from generic task management, render with slivers, express drag as raw-pointer intent using stable identities, and synchronize persistent state only from version-checked server responses. No external dependency may be added.

requirements.statement: Delete the legacy KanbanBoardView implementation, browser-renderer workarounds, and all diagnostic/fix contracts created after the original tasks-kanban-v1 contract; the rebuilt feature must have one active UI implementation and no competing legacy mechanism.

Keep the validated backend, API, persistence, authorization, immutable per-project card identity, column/card ordering contracts, optimistic concurrency expectedVersion semantics, and HTTP 409 conflict behavior unchanged.

Move Kanban presentation state out of ProjectTasksController into a dedicated ProjectKanbanController so one state owner controls project selection, board snapshots, permissions, mutation serialization, stale-response rejection, and synchronization.
Load project members, task records, and the board as one project-scoped snapshot and reject stale asynchronous responses using a selection epoch before committing UI state.

Serialize Kanban mutations. Persistent board state must remain server-authoritative: a drag/reorder expresses an intent using stable task/column IDs and expectedVersion, then replaces local state only with the accepted server response; 409 reloads the latest authoritative board.

Rebuild rendering with Flutter SDK primitives only: horizontal and vertical CustomScrollView/SliverFixedExtentList surfaces, owned ScrollControllers, fixed card extents, and raw pointer Listener events for drag intent. Do not use Draggable, DragTarget, LongPressDraggable, ReorderableListView, or the previous ListView-based board mechanism.

Compute drop targets from stable column identity and measured lane coordinates with RenderBox.globalToLocal, while keeping drag preview/target state ephemeral inside the board widget and outside persistent application state.
Rebuild ProjectKanbanPage so the top bar and board are in one bounded body render tree using SafeArea and slivers; do not use the previous Scaffold.appBar composition for the Kanban page.
Restore Flutter Web default bootstrap behavior by deleting the custom flutter_bootstrap.js and its renderer-policy test. No browser-specific rendering workaround is part of the rebuilt Kanban.
Do not add any external dependency. frontend/pubspec.yaml and its dependency set must remain unchanged; researched third-party boards are architecture references only.

Preserve user-visible Kanban capabilities: project selection, column create/rename/delete/reorder, card create/edit/delete/move, assignee management, permission gating, immutable card numbers, and conflict notices.

Add focused regression coverage for authoritative state synchronization, stale request rejection, stable identity ordering, 409 reload, native sliver rendering, raw-pointer drag intent, page geometry, interactivity, and narrow viewport bounds.

The implementation rationale is grounded in researched patterns: Flutter CustomScrollView/sliver APIs for lazy one-axis scrolling, Listener for raw pointer events, ScrollController lifecycle guidance, ChangeNotifier state encapsulation, default Flutter web bootstrap, and AppFlowy Board separation of board/group/card data and controller callbacks.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Legacy kanban_board.dart, custom web bootstrap, renderer workaround test, and the listed diagnostic POLIS contracts are absent; tasks-kanban-v1.polis.json remains.
ProjectTasksController contains no Kanban board state or Kanban mutation methods, while ProjectKanbanController exists as the sole Kanban presentation-state owner.
ProjectKanbanController uses a selection epoch, project-snapshot loading, serialized mutation tail, stable IDs, expectedVersion, and explicit 409 authoritative reload.

ProjectKanbanBoard is built with CustomScrollView and SliverFixedExtentList, owns its ScrollControllers, uses Listener/raw pointer events and coordinate-based target resolution, and contains none of the forbidden legacy drag/list primitives.
ProjectKanbanPage uses an in-body top bar, SafeArea, CustomScrollView and SliverFillRemaining, mounts ProjectKanbanBoard, and does not configure Scaffold.appBar.
No boardview, appflowy_board, kanban_board, or other new Kanban dependency is added to frontend/pubspec.yaml.
Column/card CRUD, movement, assignee actions and existing domain/API contracts remain wired through the rebuilt controller/page.
New controller, board, and page tests encode stale-response, server-authoritative move, 409 reload, stable column identity, raw-pointer drag, geometry, interaction and narrow viewport behavior.
The contract records the primary technical references used for the rebuild and treats them as design evidence rather than runtime proof.

invariants.statement: Backend source, database schema, authorization, API routes/services, Kanban contracts, and backend tests remain unchanged from baseline c6b9012a8f29e8b54ee2b2343b83c564224cc99d.
Task remains the canonical card entity; cardNumber identity and server ordering/version semantics defined by tasks-kanban-v1 remain authoritative.
No optimistic local persistence illusion is introduced: only ephemeral pointer/target feedback changes before server acceptance.
Project/task management outside the Kanban page keeps its existing behavior; only Kanban ownership is removed from ProjectTasksController.
No claim that the browser defect is fixed is valid until the rebuilt artifact is run in the real browser environment.

forbidden_states.statement: Old and new Kanban board implementations coexist.
A browser-specific CanvasKit/CPU/surface workaround is retained or added.
Draggable, DragTarget, LongPressDraggable, ReorderableListView, or the former ListView-based Kanban board is reintroduced.
ProjectTasksController remains a second Kanban state owner.
A third-party Kanban/drag-and-drop package is added.
A drag mutates the persistent visual board optimistically before the server accepts the expectedVersion write.
Backend/domain/API behavior is changed to compensate for a frontend rendering problem.

inputs.statement: Exact remote baseline: feature/tasks-kanban commit c6b9012a8f29e8b54ee2b2343b83c564224cc99d, tree e76ccd2d29461cdf00f6464ad65fb137115c51b5.
Observed defect: Chrome and Firefox both show the project/metrics area while the board body is not visibly usable, after multiple mutually different board/rendering experiments.

CI evidence before rebuild: direct widget geometry/input tests passed; later navigation tests timed out under real asynchronous page loading, so those experiments did not establish a browser rendering root cause.
Flutter pointer and scrolling references: https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/Listener-class.html and https://api.flutter.dev/flutter/widgets/ScrollController-class.html.
Flutter state reference: https://docs.flutter.dev/data-and-backend/state-mgmt/simple; Flutter Web bootstrap reference: https://docs.flutter.dev/platform-integration/web/initialization.

AppFlowy Kanban architecture reference: https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/AppFlowy-Docs/blob/main/essential-documentation/contribute-to-appflowy/architecture/frontend/database-view/kanban-board.md and source reference https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/appflowy-board. These are references only; no dependency is imported.

outputs.statement: A single rebuilt Kanban frontend composed of ProjectKanbanController, ProjectKanbanPage and ProjectKanbanBoard.
A deterministic SDK-only drag intent mechanism with stable IDs, sliver-based rendering, and server-authoritative synchronization.
Removal of historical Kanban diagnostic/rendering workarounds and restoration of default Flutter Web bootstrap behavior.
Focused tests and a versioned rebuild contract documenting the new architecture, evidence and boundaries.

failure_semantics.statement: A stale project response is ignored rather than overwriting current project state.
A 409 on card/column ordering preserves the conflict notice and reloads the latest server board instead of retaining speculative local order.
A failed non-conflict mutation propagates as an operation error; it does not silently invent a successful local board state.

If the rebuilt browser UI still reproduces the defect, this artifact does not authorize another renderer workaround; runtime paint/layout evidence must be collected against the new single implementation.
